title: GROUPING SETS
description: Learn how to use the SQL Server GROUPING SETS operator to define multiple grouping sets in a single query.

data.text: The GROUPING SETS operator is a subclause of the GROUP BY clause that allows you to define multiple grouping sets in a single query. This avoids the need for complex UNION ALL queries and improves readability and performance.
The following query creates a sales summary table that aggregates sales data by brand, category, and model year.

data.title: Create Sales Summary Table
data.content: Creates and populates the sales.sales_summary table with aggregated sales data.
data.code:
SELECT
    b.brand_name AS brand,
    c.category_name AS category,
    p.model_year,
    ROUND(
        SUM(
            quantity * i.list_price * (1 - discount)
        ),
        0
    ) AS sales
INTO sales.sales_summary
FROM
    sales.order_items i
    INNER JOIN production.products p ON p.product_id = i.product_id
    INNER JOIN production.brands b ON b.brand_id = p.brand_id
    INNER JOIN production.categories c ON c.category_id = p.category_id
GROUP BY
    b.brand_name,
    c.category_name,
    p.model_year
ORDER BY
    b.brand_name,
    c.category_name,
    p.model_year;

data.text: By definition, a grouping set is a group of columns by which you group data. A single query with an aggregate function typically defines one grouping set. GROUPING SETS allows you to define multiple grouping sets in the same query.

data.title: Single Grouping Set
data.content: A query with one grouping set: (brand, category).
data.code:
SELECT
    brand,
    category,
    SUM(sales) AS sales
FROM
    sales.sales_summary
GROUP BY
    brand,
    category
ORDER BY
    brand,
    category;

data.text: The following queries define individual grouping sets for brand, category, and the empty set (grand total).

data.title: Grouping Set by Brand
data.content: Returns sales amount grouped by brand only.
data.code:
SELECT
    brand,
    SUM(sales) AS sales
FROM
    sales.sales_summary
GROUP BY
    brand
ORDER BY
    brand;

data.title: Grouping Set by Category
data.content: Returns sales amount grouped by category only.
data.code:
SELECT
    category,
    SUM(sales) AS sales
FROM
    sales.sales_summary
GROUP BY
    category
ORDER BY
    category;

data.title: Empty Grouping Set
data.content: Returns the grand total of all sales.
data.code:
SELECT
    SUM(sales) AS sales
FROM
    sales.sales_summary;

data.alt: SQL Server GROUPING SETS empty set example

data.text: The four individual queries above return four result sets. To get a unified result set, you can use GROUPING SETS to define all grouping sets in a single query.

data.title: GROUPING SETS Syntax
data.content: Combines multiple grouping sets into one query for better readability and performance.
data.code:
SELECT
    brand,
    category,
    SUM(sales) AS sales
FROM
    sales.sales_summary
GROUP BY
    GROUPING SETS (
        (brand, category),
        (brand),
        (category),
        ()
    )
ORDER BY
    brand,
    category;

data.text: The GROUPING function indicates whether a specified column in a GROUP BY clause is aggregated or not. It returns 1 for aggregated columns and 0 for non-aggregated columns in the result set.

data.title: GROUPING Function Example
data.content: Shows which columns are aggregated in each row of the result set.
data.code:
SELECT
    GROUPING(brand) AS grouping_brand,
    GROUPING(category) AS grouping_category,
    brand,
    category,
    SUM(sales) AS sales
FROM
    sales.sales_summary
GROUP BY
    GROUPING SETS (
        (brand, category),
        (brand),
        (category),
        ()
    )
ORDER BY
    brand,
    category;

data.alt: SQL Server GROUPING SETS with GROUPING function output

items: A value of 1 means the sales amount is aggregated by that column.
A value of 0 means the sales amount is not aggregated by that column.

data.title: GROUPING SETS Key Points
points: GROUPING SETS defines multiple grouping sets in a single query.
Each grouping set is specified as a tuple of columns in parentheses.
An empty tuple () represents the grand total grouping set.
The GROUPING function helps identify which columns are aggregated in each row.
GROUPING SETS is more readable and efficient than equivalent UNION ALL queries.
